one_paragraph_summary: Panganiban profiles Justice Noel G. Tijam, Duterte's second SC appointee, who had been nominated four times by the JBC (October 5, 2009; November 29, 2009; July 28, 2010; December 9, 2011) before finally being appointed. A career jurist of almost 25 years (RTC Quezon City 1994-2003; CA 2003-2017), he finished cum laude and salutatorian at San Beda Law Class of 1971 -- with Duterte as a batch mate and Justice Secretary Aguirre as valedictorian. Critics raise two objections. On the short stint (retiring January 5, 2019): Tijam will inherit 618 cases and be raffled about 900 more over 19 active months, totaling 1,518 cases; he pledged to dispose of 1,000 during his term -- a Herculean but not impossible task. On independence: critics compare him to Marcos's classmate-appointees who legitimized one-man rule. The author responds that presidents everywhere appoint justices aligned with their programs -- what matters is adherence to the four INs (integrity, independence, industry, intelligence, with independence most important) and imperviousness to the four SHIPs (kinship, relationship, friendship, fellowship). He quotes his own 1999 book 'Leadership by Example': 'something does happen when [magistrates] don the black robes... all at once, new appointees feel a new beginning' and realize the 'god-like finality of their words and actions' immortalized in books. The author exhorts: 'He cannot afford to make mistakes because he would have no more time to correct them. He must, from Day One, be as perfect a jurist as he could be.'
